description: REQ-E5's third defense layer — the REQ-C3 adversary string-match gate — is specified as a literal grep on `strategy.json.next` for spawn-surface path strings, with no requirement for source-decoding, AST analysis, or string-construction tracing. Lines 380-382: 'REQ-C3 adversary review SHALL ALSO grep `strategy.json.next` for any string literal matching a spawn-surface path and FAIL the mutation if any match — the adversary catches the textual intent even if the OS write would have failed.' This grep is trivially defeated by any of these encodings, all of which are natural Python/shell idioms that would not raise human suspicion: (a) base64: `import base64; path = base64.b64decode('X19zaGFyZWQvbG9vcC1pbXByb3ZlLnB5').decode()` → no literal match; (b) hex: `path = bytes.fromhex('5f5f73686172656420...').decode()`; (c) template-string concatenation: `path = '_sh' + 'ared/' + 'loop-improve' + '.py'` — no substring of the joined path appears as a single literal; (d) `os.path.join('_shared', 'loop-' + 'improve.py')`; (e) glob/walk: `for f in pathlib.Path('_shared').iterdir(): ...` with conditional filter on file size or mtime; (f) reading the list of spawn-surface files FROM `spawn-surface.pinned.json` (which the spec already requires the script to read for sha verification!) and iterating that list — the spawn surface declares its own targets! PROP-E5-spawn-pin fixture (iv) tests only the naive case: 'strategy.json.next contains literal `_shared/loop-improve.py`' — none of the encoding bypasses above are in the fixture corpus, so PROP-E5 does not actually establish the property the spec claims (= 'the adversary catches the textual intent'). The spec also conflates 'adversary review' with 'grep': a fresh-context Opus adversary subagent IS capable of semantic analysis (it reads code and reasons about intent), but the spec downgrades it to a grep, which is the weakest possible mechanism. Required fix: (i) replace the grep clause with a requirement that the adversary perform Python AST + shell parse + string-flow analysis of `strategy.json.next`, tracing any value that reaches `open()`, `Path()`, `shutil`, `os.rename`, `subprocess` with shell=True, or `exec` to its sources; flag any path expression whose resolved value (after constant folding of join/format/concat) intersects the spawn-surface set; (ii) ALSO normalize candidate strings by attempting base64 decode, hex decode, URL decode before matching; (iii) update PROP-E5 fixture corpus to include each of the encoding bypasses (a)–(f) above, AND assert the adversary FAILs the mutation on every one. Without this strengthening, the third defense layer is a paper layer and the spec's 'three layers' claim is inaccurate.

evidence.snippet: REQ-C3 adversary review SHALL ALSO grep `strategy.json.next` for any string literal matching a spawn-surface path and FAIL the mutation if any match — the adversary catches the textual intent even if the OS write would have failed. These three layers (pinned-sha guard at startup, OS-level immutability, adversary string-match gate) together close ROUND-2-002 spawn-surface drift.
